products.name: Natural Stone
products.tagline: Timeless elegance, straight from the earth.
products.description: Natural stone for cladding and flooring that brings depth and character to every wall and floor. Each slab carries its own pattern, so no two spaces look alike.

content.overview: ERA natural stone comes in a wide range of varieties, each cut and finished for walls, floors and landscapes. Because every slab is formed by nature, the veining, grain and colour change from piece to piece, which gives your space a finish no printed material can copy.

features.title: Natural beauty
features.detail: Every slab carries its own veining and grain.

features.title: Durable & strong
features.detail: Hard-wearing surfaces that last for decades.

features.title: Wide range of stones
features.detail: Marble to slate, so you can match any style.

features.title: Indoor & outdoor use
features.detail: Works on facades, lobbies, patios and bathrooms.

specs.label: Varieties
specs.value: Marble, granite, sandstone, limestone, slate, quartzite, travertine

specs.label: Finishes
specs.value: Polished, honed, flamed, brushed, natural split

specs.label: Formats
specs.value: Slabs, tiles, strips and stone cladding panels

care: Seal the surface after installation, especially marble, limestone and travertine.
Clean with a pH-neutral cleaner and avoid acids.
Wipe spills quickly to prevent stains.

types.name: Marble
types.description: A metamorphic stone formed from limestone, known for flowing veins and a polished shine. Softer than granite, so it needs sealing and gentle cleaners.

types.name: Granite
types.description: An igneous stone made of quartz, feldspar and mica crystals, which gives the speckled look. Very hard and resistant to scratches, heat and weather.

types.name: Sandstone
types.description: Formed from compressed sand grains, with warm earthy tones and a natural grip. It is porous, so sealing helps outdoors.

types.name: Limestone
types.description: A calcium-rich sedimentary stone with a soft, even, pale colour and fine pits. It suits calm interiors but reacts to acids.

types.name: Slate
types.description: A fine-grained metamorphic stone that splits into thin layers. Dark tones, a naturally rough surface, and strong against water and slips.

types.name: Quartzite
types.description: Sandstone transformed by heat and pressure into very hard, dense stone with a light crystal-like shimmer. Low water absorption.

types.name: Travertine
types.description: A sedimentary stone from mineral springs, with natural bands and small pits. Stays cooler underfoot; pits come filled or unfilled.

types.name: Stone cladding
types.description: Thin split-stone pieces stacked in rows (ledgestone) to give a rough, layered 3D wall. Lighter than full stone blocks.

material.text: Natural stone forms over millions of years from minerals in the earth. It is cut from quarries and finished, but never changed into another material.

benefits.title: Lasts for decades
benefits.detail: Hard stone resists daily wear and weather.

benefits.title: Unique look
benefits.detail: No two slabs share the same pattern.

benefits.title: Adds value
benefits.detail: Stone is seen as a premium finish.

benefits.title: Cool underfoot
benefits.detail: Stays comfortable in warm climates.

guide.about: Natural stone is quarried rock cut into slabs, tiles or panels. Each type has its own hardness, porosity and look.
guide.made: Blocks are cut at the quarry, then sawn, calibrated and finished (polished, honed, flamed or brushed) in the factory.
guide.install: Fix with suitable adhesive on a level, dry base. Use movement joints on large outdoor areas.
pros: Long life when installed and sealed properly
Stays cool underfoot in hot weather
cons: Heavy, so it needs a strong base
Marble and limestone can stain or etch without sealing

faqs.q: Which stone is best for outdoors?
faqs.a: Granite, sandstone, slate and quartzite usually cope best with weather and wear. Choose a textured or flamed finish for grip.
Porous stones such as marble, limestone and travertine should be sealed. Granite and quartzite need less.
